brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Five hex bases (full at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 / -1,0 and a north half-base at 0,-1) bolted into one compact cluster, check_build ok with meshClash clear. Whether it reads as a desk is a judgement call; it is a small block cluster with no separate desktop surface or legs.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut (classic/slot s) sits on the cut face of the half-n base at 0,-1.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 (mount type) at the junction of bases 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0, the three-cell corner.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm applied to the mount spike at that junction (the solid spike was refused for platforms, so it was swapped to mount).

finish.summary: Built a small cluster of five hex bases with a drawer on the cut face of the north half-base, and a mount spike at the three-base corner (0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0) carrying a small platform. Joint bolts lock the cluster; check_build reports no errors and meshClash clear. The "desk" aspect is only loosely met since no desktop surface or legs were specified beyond the base blocks.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
